questions.q: Why did David lose his hunger at breakfast in the round-house?
choices: He was too seasick to look at any food
The only food left was cold, hard porridge
The floor was covered with glass and blood
He was afraid the food had been poisoned
questions.evidence: The floor was covered with broken glass and in a horrid mess of blood

questions.q: Why did David and Alan find it funny that the captain and Mr. Riach were shut in the fore-part of the ship?
choices: The captain had to cook his own meals for the first time
Mr. Riach had to doctor the men he had wounded himself
The two thirstiest men had only cold water to drink
The two officers had to sleep with the common sailors
questions.evidence: condemned to what they hated most--cold water

questions.q: What did Alan give David as a keepsake for the night's fighting?
choices: The dirk he had held in his left hand
A silver button cut from his coat
One of his silver-mounted pistols
A golden guinea from his money-belt
questions.evidence: cut me off one of the silver buttons from his coat

questions.q: What did Alan say would happen wherever David showed the button?
choices: The friends of Alan Breck would come around him
Any ship's captain would carry him home for free
The soldiers of King George would let him pass
The people of Appin would give him food and a bed
questions.evidence: the friends of Alan Breck will come around you

questions.q: What did David have to be careful not to do when Alan boasted?
choices: Tell him that his coat was spoiled and worn out
Ask him questions about his chief and the gold
Remind him that the captain had beaten him at cards
Smile at his vanity, which could start a quarrel
questions.evidence: I was always in danger of smiling at his vanity

questions.q: Why did David value the button more after watching Alan brush his coat?
choices: Alan told him the buttons were made of pure gold from France
Alan offered to sew the button onto David's own jacket
Alan said it was the last button his father had ever owned
Alan took such care of the coat, yet cut a button from it for him
questions.evidence: I put a higher value on his gift

questions.q: What did Mr. Riach admit when he came to ask for a parley?
choices: That he had been paid by David's uncle to watch over him
That he was frightened, and the men would not follow anyway
That the captain was dead and he was now in command
That he had a plan to help David and Alan escape at night

questions.q: How did the captain look when he came to the window to talk?
choices: Angry and red, waving a cutlass about
Stern and pale, with his arm in a sling
Calm and smiling, with a bottle in hand
Weak and lying on a blanket on the deck
questions.evidence: with his arm in a sling, and looking stern and pale

questions.q: Why did Alan refuse to trust the captain's word?
choices: The captain had given his hand on a bargain the night before and then attacked
The captain was known to be a Campbell and an enemy of Alan's clan
The captain had once handed another Jacobite over to the soldiers at Glasgow
The captain had lied about the brig being bound for the Carolinas
questions.evidence: I doubt your word is a breakable

questions.q: Alan says his people pass between islands in "their bit cobles." Using the note in the text, what is a "coble"?
choices: A pony for riding hills
A small fishing boat
A rough woollen cloak
A wooden walking stick
questions.evidence: a small boat used in fishing

questions.q: Where did Alan say he would not be set ashore?
choices: In Appin, Ardgour or Morven
Within thirty miles of his home
Anywhere near Arisaig or Morar
In a country of the Campbells
questions.evidence: except in a country of the Campbells

questions.q: What was the last part of the treaty between Alan and the captain?
choices: Half of the gold to be paid before they left the ship
A promise that David would be set free in Glasgow
The return of Mr. Shuan's body to his wife in Leith
A bottle of brandy traded for two buckets of water
questions.evidence: a bottle of brandy against two buckets of water

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David asking the captain to take him home to the house of Shaws
Alan and the beaten captain making terms to set Alan ashore
Alan and David taking over the brig and sailing it to France
The captain and his crew winning back the round-house by a trick
questions.evidence: That was the last clause of the treaty
